definitions.explanation: An allergic reaction to pollen, causing symptoms like sneezing, runny nose, and itchy eyes. Extremely common in Japan, especially during spring cedar pollen season.

examples.japanese: {春|はる}になると{花粉症|かふんしょう}の{症状|しょうじょう}が{出|で}る。
examples.english: When spring comes, my hay fever symptoms appear.

examples.japanese: {花粉症|かふんしょう}がひどくて{外|そと}に{出|で}られない。
examples.english: My hay fever is so bad that I can't go outside.

examples.japanese: {日本人|にほんじん}の{約|やく}4{人|にん}に1{人|にん}が{花粉症|かふんしょう}だと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: It's said that about 1 in 4 Japanese people have hay fever.

notes:
{花粉症|かふんしょう} refers to pollen allergies (hay fever).

Common symptoms:
- くしゃみ (sneezing)
- {鼻水|はなみず} (runny nose)
- {鼻|はな}づまり (stuffy nose)
- {目|め}の{痒|かゆ}み (itchy eyes)
- {涙|なみだ} (watery eyes)

Main allergens in Japan:
- {杉|すぎ}{花粉|かふん} (cedar pollen - February to April)
- {檜|ひのき}{花粉|かふん} (cypress pollen - March to May)
- {稲|いね}{科|か}{花粉|かふん} (grass pollen - May to July)
- {秋|あき}の{雑草|ざっそう}{花粉|かふん} (autumn weed pollen)

Common expressions:
- {花粉症|かふんしょう}の{薬|くすり} (hay fever medicine)
- {花粉症|かふんしょう}{対策|たいさく} (hay fever countermeasures)

Cultural note:
{花粉症|かふんしょう} affects a huge portion of the Japanese population. During peak season, many people wear masks and special glasses. Weather forecasts include pollen counts ({花粉|かふん}{予報|よほう}), and pharmacies prominently display {花粉症|かふんしょう} remedies.
